This revised version of my old Autopistol STL has some subtle changes that I like. I also added a few variants with different hands attached for easy conversions. In a grimdark science fantasy universe such a weapon as this might be found in the hands of chaotic cultists, undercity gang members, Imperial officials, militia troopers, organized criminals, xeno cultists, merchants and their guards, household troops, and many more. For physically converting or digitally remixing miniatures this one pistol has many potential uses.

I made some changes to my existing Autopistol Model 302 STL. I took most of my inspiration for the original design from a couple images I found online. I liked the look overall, though I felt like the end of the barrel was maybe inclined to break off if dropped. So for this version I changed the proportions so that the muzzle break in front of the weapon connected very slightly to the angled front of the forward handgrip on the pistol. Looking at other images online, I also decided to shorten the pistol's ammo magazine. Previously the magazine extended below the pistol grip, but now it stops just short of being equal in length to the pistol grip. The width and height of the pistol remain the same, but I shortened the overall length from 12mm to 11.5mm which I think makes it scaled a bit better for most plastic, resin, and STL miniatures out there.

Rigged version of an ork made by VidovicArts. I used this to create all my ork models so far.

There are a some hidden parts in the file and lots of poses in the pose library of the rig. My workflow with this is as follows:

-Add objects like torsi an weapons to the file an pot them to the right place at the body
-hide all parts you don't need for your boi
-make copy of the rig, the body and all parts you added
-parent all objects to the rig (as objects to specific bones)
-choose a pose from the pose library or create a new one.
-apply all modifiers to the parts
-unparent all objects while keeping their transformation
-boolean unite all objects
-use windows 3D builder to repair any problems in the mesh
-print

These STL files are designed to equip my [Sculptris Dummies](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1972042). You won't be able to import these files into Sculptris, though once you get your character posed, you can align these parts in any model staging platform (MakerBot Deskto, Blender, Meshmixer, or 3D Builder are all good choices). All of these parts are also available in Andrew Stockton's awesome [Desktop Hero](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/263291121/desktophero-free-3d-printable-character-maker) project as well (which is quite a bit easier than adjusting all the parts by hand). All of these weapons have been scaled to 28mm/Heroic scale, so they should be ready for any kind of miniature conversion if you want to print them separately.

If you make anything with these (including through Desktop Hero), let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested in helping to fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want!
